briefs.topic: Running Autonomous AI Agents in Docker
briefs.target_angle: Focus on the 'how-to' security and isolation aspect for developers who are afraid to run AI agents on their main machine.
briefs.why_it_works: The data shows a massive appetite for 'AI Agent' and 'Isolation' content, with AI Fusion's viral video proving that small channels can achieve a 129.4x outperformance ratio by focusing on the specific capability of autonomous agents. By combining the high-utility technical focus of the Red Hat and Cloud Codes videos with the accessible 'self-hosted' framing of Better Creating, you provide a high-value solution to a common developer fear.
pattern_insights: High outperformance is driven by specific technical utility (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, Sandboxing) rather than general AI news.
Small channels win when they solve a specific 'fear' (like AI hackers or credential leaks) rather than just showcasing general AI agent capabilities.
The most successful videos frame AI agents as a tangible tool that needs to be 'contained' or 'deployed' safely.
Titles that focus on a specific transition (e.g., switching from Python to Docker) or a specific constraint (e.g., sandboxing) perform significantly better than generic AI overviews.

briefs.hook_script: Most people are running AI agents directly on their host machines, which is honestly a disaster waiting to happen. If you've seen the recent news about autonomous agents acting on their own, you know why isolation matters. Today, I'm going to show you exactly how to containerize your agents using Docker so they can do the heavy lifting without ever touching your sensitive system files.

thumbnail_direction.primary_image: A split screen showing a scary terminal command on one side and a clean Docker logo on the other.
thumbnail_direction.focal_point: A glowing shield icon over a Docker container

pacing_outline.action: Demonstrate a simple AI agent script and explain the risk of it having unrestricted system access.
Briefly explain the concept of sandboxing, referencing the logic seen in the AI Engineer and Cloud Codes videos.
Step-by-step screen share of setting up the Dockerfile and environment variables for the agent.
Run a harmless but 'agentic' task inside the container to prove it works and is isolated.

production_checklist: Verify Docker is installed on the host machine
Create a simple AI agent script that requires file system access
Prepare a clean Dockerfile that limits permissions
Record screen captures of the container logs to show isolation
